about: Spec 3.11.0 (acp.md, *An editor as the client*). `kind: trim` — `_lembas/complete`: `prefix` and `suffix` cut to `max` UTF-8 bytes each, the prefix keeping its end and the suffix its start, at a character boundary. `kind: context` — the block a prompt's `_meta.lembas.editor` becomes in the user message (`block: null`: none); `root` is the session's project, `limits` override `loop.json` `editor.context` for the case. `kind: message` — the user message of a rewrite (`_lembas/edit`) from its params; `limits` override `editor.rewrite`'s context limits. `kind: output` — what a rewrite answers from what the model streamed in `chunks`, for a selection `selection`: a fence around the whole answer taken off, and the end made the selection's; the pieces sent as `_lembas/edit/delta` joined are that text. `kind: model` — the model a rewrite runs on: `asked` (its `model`), `session` (the model of the session it names), `main` (the person's main model on the server), `served` (the login's models), `start` (what a new session in the directory would start on). `kind: diff` — what the content of an approval card (`when: ask`) or of a finished edit's update (`when: done`) is made of, for a client that said `editor: true` or not, the texts being `bytes` together against `max`. `kind: buffer` — unsaved text: where a tool that changes a file takes its text from (`read`: the client gave `text`, `fails`, or offers `none`; `tracked`: the session read the file through the client before), and where a write goes (`write`: `taken`, `refused`, `unknown` — no answer — or `none`: the client does not write; `unsaved`: the editor's text for the file, asked once more, is not the disk's). CLI: src/acp/editor.ts, src/tool/buffers.ts.

cases.about: Both short: sent as they are.
A long prefix keeps its end — the text nearest the cursor.
A long suffix keeps its start.
Bytes, cut at a character boundary: three bytes of two two-byte characters are one character.
Everything said: one block, each line in its place; the file in front is not repeated among the open ones.

cases.about: A path is one line of plain text: control characters, line breaks and angle brackets are taken out of it, so a file's name cannot close the block.

Text of a file's or a tool's own cannot close the block: a closing tag of the block or of the selection inside a diagnostic or the selected text is written with a space after `<`. Nothing else of it is touched — `Array<string>` stays.

cases.about: Only the selection and the instruction; a selection with no line break at its end is closed on a new line all the same.
A language without a path.
The context is trimmed towards the selection: `before` keeps its last lines, `after` its first.
…and by bytes, at a line where one fits.
Plain text, streamed in pieces.
A fence around the whole answer is taken off, however it is cut into pieces.
The selection had no line break at its end: neither has the replacement.
The selection ended with a line break the model left out: put back.
Several line breaks at the end become the selection's one.
Backticks that are not the first line are content.
Inside a fenced answer only the last line's fence closes it.
Indentation at the start is the replacement's own.
Blank lines before a fence go with it.
A fence the model never closed: its opening line is still dropped.
Nothing but a fence is no text.
The model asked for, whatever else is known — the server decides whether it exists.
The session's model before the person's main model.
No session: the person's main model.
A main model the login no longer serves is skipped.
Nothing chosen: as a new session in the directory would start.
An editor is asked about an edit: the change as diff items.
Any other client: the unified diff as text, as before.
Too much text for items: the unified diff as text.
An edit that ran, to an editor: the tool's output, then the items.
An edit that ran, to any other client: the output alone.
An edit that ran, too large for items: the output alone.
The editor gave the file's text: that is the text.
The client offers no reading: the disk.
The editor did not answer for a file the session never read there: the disk, as before.
The editor did not answer for a file the session read there: refused — its buffer may hold what is not saved, and the disk's text would be written over it.
The client took the write.
The client refused a file the session never read there: the device writes the disk.
The client refused a file the session read there: nothing is written behind its back.
No answer in time: the client may still apply it — never written to the disk as well.
The client offers no writing: the disk.
A client that reads but does not write, a file the session read there, and the editor's text is what is on disk: nothing is unsaved — the device writes the disk.
…and the editor holds text that is not saved: refused, with a sentence asking for the file to be saved first.
